source_meta._title: Dispensing a Bucket of Tadpole above or below a dimension dispenses the item, instead of a tadpole

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 22w11a in a single-player Creative-mode world with commands/cheats enabled. Perform the reproduction in the Nether. No dedicated server, specific world seed, datapack, resource pack, or nondefault graphics setting is required by the report.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact Java Edition snapshot 22w11a rather than the fix version 22w13a.
Create or load a world in Creative mode with commands/cheats enabled so the supplied /setblock and /tp commands can be executed.
Have one Dispenser, one Stone Button, one Bucket of Axolotl, and one Bucket of Tadpole available from the Creative inventory.
If using a manually constructed Nether portal, also have 14 Obsidian and one Flint and Steel.
Use only one mob bucket in the dispenser at a time. Before testing the Bucket of Tadpole, remove the empty bucket left by the axolotl control activation so dispenser slot selection is deterministic.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation that uses snapshot 22w11a, launch it, and wait for the main menu to appear. Confirm that the displayed version is 22w11a before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft Java Edition main menu is open and identifies the running version as 22w11a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer and create a new world. Set Game Mode to Creative and ensure commands/cheats are enabled, then create the world and wait until terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a loaded Creative-mode world and can execute commands.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab to obtain one Dispenser, one Stone Button, one Bucket of Axolotl, one Bucket of Tadpole, 14 Obsidian, and one Flint and Steel. Place them in accessible inventory or hotbar slots, then close the inventory with E or Esc.
steps.exact_input: Dispenser; Stone Button; Bucket of Axolotl; Bucket of Tadpole; Obsidian; Flint and Steel
steps.success_cue: All required dispenser-test items and Nether-portal materials are present in the player's inventory.

steps.action: In an open area, build a vertical Nether portal frame from Obsidian. Make the outside of the rectangle 4 blocks wide and 5 blocks tall, leaving a 2-block-wide by 3-block-tall empty opening inside the frame.
steps.success_cue: A complete upright Obsidian rectangle with a 2-by-3-block empty interior is present.

steps.action: Select Flint and Steel in the active hotbar slot and use it with right-click on an Obsidian block along the inside bottom of the frame.
steps.success_cue: The portal interior is filled with the animated purple Nether portal field.

steps.action: Walk into the purple portal field and remain inside it until dimension travel begins.
steps.success_cue: The Nether loading screen or dimension transition begins.

steps.action: Wait until the Nether terrain has rendered and normal movement and inventory interaction respond again. If necessary, verify the Nether by its red-toned terrain and Nether ambience.
steps.success_cue: The player is fully loaded in the Nether and can move normally.

steps.action: Enable Creative flight by double-tapping the Jump control, which is Space by default. Rise slightly to confirm that flight is active; this prevents an unintended fall while working at the upper dimension boundary.
steps.exact_input: Space twice
steps.success_cue: The player can hover without standing on a block.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, type the report's setblock command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter. Execute it as the player, not from a server console.
steps.exact_input: /setblock ~ 255 ~ dispenser[facing=up]
steps.success_cue: The command completes without a red syntax or permission error, placing an upward-facing dispenser at the player's current X and Z coordinates and Y=255.

steps.action: Press T to open chat again, type the report's teleport command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is teleported to Y=256 while retaining the same X and Z coordinates.

steps.action: Wait until movement and rendering respond normally after teleportation. If needed, press F3 to confirm the player's Y coordinate is approximately 256, then close the debug display with F3. Look downward to locate the dispenser directly below at Y=255.
steps.exact_input: F3
steps.success_cue: The player is hovering at the Nether's upper boundary and the upward-facing dispenser is directly below or immediately adjacent.

steps.action: While remaining in Creative flight, move horizontally far enough to see and target a side or the top face of the dispenser without drifting away from it.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair can be placed on a visible face of the dispenser.

steps.action: Use right-click on the dispenser to open its inventory. Confirm that all nine dispenser slots are empty before adding the control item.
steps.success_cue: The Dispenser interface is open and its nine storage slots are empty.

steps.action: In the open Dispenser interface, click the Bucket of Axolotl in the player inventory and then click one empty dispenser slot to place it there. Do not add the Bucket of Tadpole yet. Press Esc to close the interface.
steps.success_cue: The dispenser contains only one Bucket of Axolotl and the interface is closed.

steps.action: Select the Stone Button in the hotbar. Aim at a vertical side face of the dispenser and right-click to attach the button. Leave at least one other dispenser face accessible for reopening its inventory.
steps.success_cue: A button is attached to the side of the dispenser and can be targeted with the crosshair.

steps.action: Aim at the attached button and right-click it once to activate the dispenser for the axolotl control trial. Allow the button to release before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The dispenser has activated once, an axolotl has been released above it, and the button has returned to its unpressed state.

steps.action: Aim at a dispenser face that is not occupied by the button and right-click to reopen the Dispenser interface.
steps.success_cue: The Dispenser interface is open after the axolotl control activation.

steps.action: Remove every item remaining in the dispenser, including the empty bucket produced by the control activation. Shift-clicking the remaining item transfers it to the player inventory. Confirm that all nine dispenser slots are empty.
steps.success_cue: All nine dispenser slots are empty, preventing a residual item from being randomly selected during the tadpole trial.

steps.action: While the Dispenser interface remains open, click the Bucket of Tadpole in the player inventory and then click one empty dispenser slot to place it there. Do not place any other item in the dispenser.
steps.success_cue: The Bucket of Tadpole is the dispenser's only stored item.

steps.action: Press Esc to close the Dispenser interface. Keep the player hovering close enough to target the attached button.
steps.success_cue: The dispenser interface is closed, the dispenser contains only the Bucket of Tadpole, and the button is visible and reachable.

steps.action: Aim directly at the attached button and right-click it exactly once to activate the dispenser with the Bucket of Tadpole. Do not activate it repeatedly; hand off immediately after this activation.
steps.success_cue: The button has just been pressed and the dispenser has begun its single tadpole-bucket activation.

stor.handoff_condition: The upward-facing dispenser at Y=255 in the Nether has just been activated once while containing only one Bucket of Tadpole, with the player positioned at the upper dimension boundary. Begin observation immediately after this activation.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, or world-generation settings. Creative mode with cheats enabled is selected as the simplest deterministic way to obtain the items and execute the supplied commands.

The report only says to enter the Nether and does not prescribe a portal or command-based travel method. A manually constructed Nether portal is used to avoid introducing an additional version-sensitive dimension command.
The report specifies activation with a button but does not identify the button material. A Stone Button is selected as a practical implementation choice; no button type is stated as required.
A comment states that the issue occurs in all dimensions, but the original reproduction explicitly uses the Nether. This plan preserves the original Nether procedure.
No external verification was needed because the report supplies the affected snapshots, exact commands, dimension, item order, dispenser orientation, and trigger action.

source_meta._title: Items glitch inside the piston head when pushed through powder snow or cobwebs

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.14 in single-player, using a fresh copy of the attached prebuilt world "Item glitch bug world download.zip". Use the cobweb-based apparatus provided in that world; powder snow does not exist in Minecraft 1.14. Do not use the listed fix version, 1.21.10 Release Candidate 1.
preconditions: Obtain the report attachment named "Item glitch bug world download.zip"; the report does not provide enough coordinates, commands, or construction details to recreate its special piston setup independently.
Install and launch the exact affected release Minecraft Java Edition 1.14, corresponding to the first listed affected version "Minecraft 1.14".
Extract the attached ZIP into the Java Edition saves directory. The extracted world folder must directly contain level.dat rather than containing an extra nested folder above level.dat.
Use a fresh copy of the attached world so the piston begins in the state intended by the reporter and no item entities remain from an earlier attempt.
Leave the command blocks, cobweb, piston, redstone wiring, and item path in their supplied positions. Do not substitute powder snow in this 1.14 reproduction.
Use the world's prebuilt redstone controls where available. The report does not supply the commands stored in the command blocks, so do not clear or edit their contents.

steps.action: With Minecraft closed, extract "Item glitch bug world download.zip" into the Minecraft Java Edition saves directory. If extraction creates an outer folder containing a second world folder, move the inner folder—the one containing level.dat—directly into the saves directory.
steps.exact_input: Item glitch bug world download.zip
steps.success_cue: A single world folder is present under the saves directory, and level.dat is directly inside that world folder.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher and select or create a Java Edition installation that runs the exact release 1.14. Do not select 1.14.1 or another nearby release.
steps.success_cue: The launcher installation selected for play explicitly shows version 1.14.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft Java Edition using the 1.14 installation and wait for the title screen to finish loading.
steps.exact_input: Play
steps.success_cue: The lower-left title-screen version label identifies Minecraft 1.14.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose the imported world from the attachment, and open it. If several similarly named copies exist, choose the fresh, unused copy extracted for this attempt.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> imported attached world -> Play Selected World
steps.success_cue: The player has entered the attached test world.

steps.action: Wait without operating any redstone until the surrounding chunks and the test apparatus have rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The nearby blocks are fully rendered, movement is responsive, and the test apparatus can be inspected without additional terrain loading.

steps.action: Locate the prebuilt test apparatus in the attached world. Identify its command blocks, the area containing cobweb, the piston aimed toward or through that area, and the separate redstone controls used to power the command blocks and the piston. Inspect the controls without activating them yet.
steps.success_cue: The command-block power control and piston power control have both been identified, and the cobweb is visible in the piston's item path.

steps.action: Confirm that this is an unused initial setup: the piston must be retracted and there must not already be leftover item entities from an earlier attempt in the apparatus. If the setup is not fresh, exit without saving and restore another fresh copy from the ZIP rather than attempting an undocumented manual reset.
steps.success_cue: The piston is retracted, the cobweb apparatus is intact, and no leftover test items are present.

steps.action: Supply redstone power to the prebuilt command blocks using the world’s provided command-block control. For a button or lever, aim at it and use the Use/Place Block action, which is right-click by default. Activate the supplied control only once unless the world clearly provides one separate control for each command block; in that case, activate each intended command-block control once. Do not open or edit the command blocks.
steps.exact_input: Use/Place Block (default: right-click) on the command-block power control
steps.success_cue: The command blocks have run and multiple dropped-item entities are visible in the cobweb portion of the apparatus.

steps.action: Allow the newly summoned item entities to enter or remain inside the cobweb in front of the retracted piston. Continue as soon as the multiple items are visibly present in the intended cobweb position; do not repeatedly summon additional batches.
steps.success_cue: Multiple dropped-item entities are simultaneously inside the cobweb in the piston's path, and the piston remains retracted.

steps.action: Aim at the separate control that powers the piston and activate it once with the Use/Place Block action. Do not repeatedly cycle the piston. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately after the piston extends and pushes the item entities through or from the cobweb.
steps.exact_input: Use/Place Block (default: right-click) on the piston power control
steps.success_cue: The piston has just extended once, its head has entered the item path, and the item entities have just been acted upon by the moving piston.

stor.handoff_condition: The piston has just been powered for one extension while multiple summoned item entities occupy the cobweb in its path. Begin observation immediately, without cycling the piston again or disturbing the items.
uncertainties: The attached world file itself was not supplied with the report text. Execution therefore depends on separately obtaining "Item glitch bug world download.zip" from the Mojira attachment.

The report does not provide the world seed, coordinates, stored command text, command-block arrangement, redstone-control type, or a manual construction schematic. Those details must be taken unchanged from the attached world.

The phrase "under some special conditions" is not expanded in the written report. This plan preserves those conditions by requiring the supplied prebuilt world rather than attempting to infer or rebuild the apparatus.

The report says to "Power the command blocks" and then "Power the piston" but does not identify the exact buttons, levers, pressure plates, or other redstone inputs. The executor must distinguish the controls by inspecting their wiring and must activate the command-block control before the piston control.
Although 24w45a is also listed as affected, Minecraft 1.14 is selected because it is the first affected version listed, as required. The 1.14 reproduction must use cobweb rather than powder snow.

source_meta._title: Some piston operations don't send neighbor updates

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 25w03a in a vanilla single-player Creative Mode superflat world. Use default controls unless an action binding has been changed. No seed, coordinates, server, datapack, resource pack, mod, or command is specified by the report.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected snapshot 25w03a, not a later snapshot.
Use a newly created Creative Mode world so the required redstone components can be obtained without crafting.
Find a clear, level area at least 5 blocks long and 3 blocks wide, with no nearby redstone components that could update the test circuit.

The reproduction uses one regular piston, two levers, and one redstone dust. A regular piston is selected as the simplest interpretation because the attachment itself is not available in the supplied report.
Identify two roles for the levers: the target lever will be destroyed by the piston, while the rear activation lever will trigger the piston.

All circuit components must be placed on top of the same level floor. The target lever must occupy the block space immediately in front of the piston, and the redstone dust must be horizontally adjacent to that target lever.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation for the exact Java Edition snapshot listed by the report, and start the game with that installation.
steps.exact_input: Minecraft Launcher -> Installations -> New installation (if needed) -> Version: snapshot 25w03a -> Create/Save -> Play
steps.success_cue: The title screen displays Minecraft Java Edition 25w03a.

steps.action: Create a disposable single-player Creative Mode superflat world. No particular seed is required. Superflat is an execution convenience and is not stated as a bug requirement.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> set Game Mode to Creative -> World settings/options -> World Type: Superflat -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player spawns in a Creative Mode world with a broad, level surface.

steps.action: Wait before building until world loading has finished.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, the player can move and look around normally, and opening the inventory responds without loading pauses.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory and place one regular Piston, two Levers, and Redstone Dust into separate hotbar slots. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots along the bottom of the screen; selecting a slot makes that item the active held item.
steps.exact_input: Press E -> use the Search Items tab if necessary -> search for and move "Piston", "Lever", and "Redstone Dust" to the hotbar -> press E to close the inventory
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains a regular piston, at least two levers, and redstone dust.

steps.action: Choose a clear section of the flat floor at least 5 blocks long and 3 blocks wide. Remove any grass, flowers, or other non-floor blocks from the area so they cannot interfere with placement or updates.
steps.exact_input: Select an empty hotbar slot and left-click any obstructing plants or blocks in the chosen area.
steps.success_cue: A clear, level test area with no existing redstone components is available.

steps.action: Place the regular piston horizontally on top of the floor. Stand on the side that will become the front of the circuit and place the piston so its wooden pushing face points toward the player and into an empty block space. Leave at least two empty floor positions both in front of and behind it.
steps.exact_input: Select the Piston hotbar slot -> stand in the intended front direction -> right-click the top of the floor block where the piston base should be placed
steps.success_cue: A horizontal piston is present, and its wooden face points into an empty space above the neighboring floor block.

steps.action: Designate the empty block space directly in front of the piston's wooden face as the target position. The piston must be able to extend into this exact position without encountering a solid block.
steps.success_cue: The block directly in front of the piston is empty and has a solid floor block beneath it.

steps.action: Place the target lever on top of the floor block directly in front of the piston. Approach from the side if necessary so the player does not occupy the target position while placing it. This must be a floor-mounted lever occupying the block space into which the piston will extend.
steps.exact_input: Select the Lever hotbar slot -> right-click the top face of the floor block immediately in front of the piston
steps.success_cue: A floor-mounted lever occupies the single block immediately in front of the piston face, while the piston remains retracted.

steps.action: Place one redstone dust on the floor block immediately to either horizontal side of the target lever, at the same height. Do not place the dust in front of or behind the piston, and do not create a longer redstone line.
steps.exact_input: Select Redstone Dust in the hotbar -> right-click the top of either floor block directly beside the target lever
steps.success_cue: One unpowered redstone dust is horizontally adjacent to the target lever and is not adjacent to the back of the piston.

steps.action: Place the rear activation lever on top of the floor block immediately behind the piston, centered with the piston and target lever. Leave this newly placed lever in its default off position. The resulting top-down center line must be: rear activation lever, piston facing forward, target lever. The redstone dust must be one block to the side of the target lever.
steps.exact_input: Select the Lever hotbar slot -> right-click the top face of the floor block immediately behind the piston
steps.success_cue: The rear activation lever is directly behind the piston and is off; the piston is still retracted; the target lever and adjacent dust remain in place.

steps.action: Right-click the target lever directly in front of the piston once to switch that lever on. Do not operate the rear activation lever yet.
steps.exact_input: Aim at the target lever -> right-click once
steps.success_cue: The target lever is visibly switched on, the adjacent redstone dust is brightly powered, and the piston remains retracted.

steps.action: Pause briefly without placing, breaking, or operating anything. Confirm that the initial powered state is stable before triggering the piston.
steps.exact_input: Wait approximately 1 second without input.
steps.success_cue: The target lever remains present and on, the neighboring redstone dust remains powered, the rear activation lever remains off, and the piston remains retracted.

steps.action: Move to a position where the rear activation lever can be operated without clicking the piston or disturbing the target lever or redstone dust. Aim the crosshair at the rear activation lever.
steps.exact_input: Use W/A/S/D as needed -> position the crosshair over the rear activation lever behind the piston
steps.success_cue: The crosshair targets the rear activation lever while the target lever is still on and its adjacent redstone dust is powered.

steps.action: Trigger the reproduction by right-clicking the rear activation lever exactly once. Allow the piston to complete its first extension into the target lever's block space. Do not toggle the rear lever again and do not touch any other block after the extension.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once on the rear activation lever.
steps.success_cue: The rear activation lever is on, the piston has completed its extension, and the target lever directly in front of it has been destroyed. No additional player action has occurred.

stor.handoff_condition: The rear activation lever has just been switched on, the piston has completed its first extension into the former target-lever position, and the target lever has been destroyed. Leave the circuit untouched and immediately transfer control to the observation subsystem without evaluating or changing the redstone dust.
uncertainties: The formal report provides no textual construction sequence and instead refers to the attached video, missing_neighbor_updates_on_piston_breaking_lever.mp4. The attachment's visual instructions were not accessible, so its exact orientation and block layout could not be recovered.

The use of a regular piston, a floor-mounted target lever directly in front of it, adjacent redstone dust, and a separate rear activation lever is a minimum deterministic reconstruction supported by the description and attachment filename, but may not exactly match the video.

The report does not specify game mode, world type, seed, coordinates, or multiplayer requirements. Creative Mode, a superflat world, and single-player are practical execution choices rather than reported requirements.

If the inaccessible video uses a sticky piston, wall-mounted lever, different activation source, or another precise orientation, this plan may need to be adjusted to match that attachment before execution.

source_meta._title: Changing a powered Command block from impulse/chain mode to repeat mode doesn't trigger it until repowering

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition Minecraft 15w34b, unmodified client, single-player integrated server, Creative mode, cheats enabled, preferably an English-language UI and a Superflat world. Default keyboard and mouse controls are assumed: T for chat, number keys or mouse wheel for hotbar selection, right-click for Use/Place, and Left Shift for Sneak.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact historical Java Edition snapshot Minecraft 15w34b in a separate launcher installation so newer worlds are not opened accidentally.
Use a newly created single-player Creative world with cheats enabled. No specific seed or coordinates are required.
Ensure the player has permission to execute commands and edit command blocks; enabling cheats in this single-player world supplies the required permission.
Use an open, loaded area with a solid floor and enough room to place and access one command block.
Do not use the report's fix version 19w41a.
Leave command feedback at its new-world default so the harmless test command can be confirmed from chat.
Do not toggle or otherwise interrupt the lever's power after the initial impulse execution; continuous power through the mode change is the key test condition.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select and start the exact Java Edition installation for Minecraft 15w34b. Do not substitute a later affected version or the fix version.
steps.exact_input: Minecraft 15w34b
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu has loaded and displays version 15w34b.

steps.action: Create a new single-player test world. Select Creative game mode, open More World Options, set Allow Cheats to ON, and select the Superflat world type to provide a deterministic open building area. Then create the world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options... -> Allow Cheats: ON -> World Type: Superflat -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a new Creative-mode world on a flat surface.

steps.action: Wait before building until the nearby terrain has rendered and player movement and controls respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The ground around the player is fully rendered and the player can move and look around without world-loading pauses.

steps.action: Obtain one command block. Press T to open in-game chat, type the exact command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.exact_input: /give @p minecraft:command_block 1
steps.success_cue: A command block item appears in the player's inventory or hotbar, and the command reports that the item was given successfully.

steps.action: Obtain one lever. Press T to open in-game chat again, type the exact command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.exact_input: /give @p minecraft:lever 1
steps.success_cue: A lever item appears in the player's inventory or hotbar, and the command reports that the item was given successfully.

steps.action: Select the command block in the hotbar. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen; use the corresponding number key or the mouse wheel until the command block is outlined as the active item.
steps.exact_input: Select the hotbar slot containing minecraft:command_block
steps.success_cue: The command block is visible in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Aim at the top of a solid floor block directly in front of the player and right-click once to place the command block.
steps.exact_input: right-click
steps.success_cue: One orange impulse command block is placed on the floor and has at least one exposed side that the player can target.

steps.action: Aim at an exposed face of the command block and right-click to open its configuration interface.
steps.exact_input: right-click
steps.success_cue: The command block configuration interface is open and contains a command-entry field and a block-type control.

steps.action: Click the command-entry field and enter the harmless deterministic test command exactly as shown, without a leading slash.
steps.exact_input: say MC-86846
steps.success_cue: The command field contains exactly "say MC-86846".

steps.action: Confirm that the command block type is Impulse. If the type control does not currently show Impulse, click it until it does. Do not change the command block to Repeat yet.
steps.exact_input: Impulse
steps.success_cue: The type control in the command block interface reads Impulse.

steps.action: Click Done to save the command while the block is still an impulse command block and return to the world.
steps.exact_input: Done
steps.success_cue: The interface closes, the orange impulse command block remains placed, and no power source is attached yet.

steps.action: Select the lever in the hotbar using its number key or the mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: Select the hotbar slot containing minecraft:lever
steps.success_cue: The lever is visible in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Attach the lever directly to the top of the command block. Because right-clicking a command block normally opens its interface, hold the Sneak control, whose default key is Left Shift, while right-clicking the command block's top face. Release Left Shift after the lever is placed.
steps.exact_input: Hold Left Shift + right-click the top face of the command block
steps.success_cue: A lever is visibly attached to the top of the command block, and the command block interface is not open.

steps.action: Aim directly at the attached lever and right-click it once to switch it on. Do not turn it off during any later step.
steps.exact_input: right-click the lever once
steps.success_cue: The lever handle moves to its powered position and a chat line containing "MC-86846" appears, confirming that the impulse command block executed once while becoming powered.

steps.action: While the lever remains on, aim at an exposed side face of the command block rather than at the lever, and right-click to reopen the command block configuration interface. Do not touch the lever first.
steps.exact_input: right-click an exposed side face of the powered command block
steps.success_cue: The command block configuration interface is open, the command field still contains "say MC-86846", and no action has been taken to remove or toggle the lever's power.

steps.action: Use the command block type control to change the block from Impulse to Repeat. Click the type control as many times as required until its displayed type is Repeat. Do not close the interface until Repeat is visibly selected, and do not change the command text.
steps.exact_input: Repeat
steps.success_cue: The command block type control reads Repeat and the command field still contains exactly "say MC-86846".

steps.action: Click Done to commit the change from Impulse to Repeat while the same lever has remained continuously on. Immediately hand control to the observation subsystem; do not toggle the lever, place or break neighboring blocks, reopen the command block interface, or otherwise update the setup.
steps.exact_input: Done
steps.success_cue: The configuration interface has just closed, the command block is in its purple Repeat form, and the attached lever remains in the same powered position without having been toggled off and on.

stor.handoff_condition: The command block has just been committed from Impulse mode to Repeat mode by clicking Done while its attached lever remained continuously on from the initial impulse execution. Begin observation immediately, without repowering the block or causing any additional block update.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, terrain type, or dedicated-server requirement. A fresh single-player Superflat Creative world is therefore used as a practical deterministic setup.
The report does not prescribe a particular command. The harmless command "say MC-86846" is used because one execution is easy to confirm in chat and it does not modify the world or player state.
The report does not prescribe the redstone power source. A lever attached directly to the command block is used because it can provide visibly continuous power throughout the mode change.

Minecraft 15w34b is the first listed affected version and is therefore selected. The later Always Active reproduction variant is not used because external version-history information indicates that the Always Active/Needs Redstone UI option was added after 15w34b; the original continuously redstone-powered variant is applicable to the recommended version.
Comment 19 mentions Minecraft 1.17.1, but that version is not present in the report's Affects versions field and has therefore not been added to affected_versions.

The exact translated wording and visual placement of the historical command-block type control may vary with the selected language, but the executor must identify the control whose displayed state cycles among Impulse, Chain, and Repeat.

source_meta._title: Ender dragon and piglin heads are not activated when powered by comparators

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition client running the exact snapshot Minecraft 15w34c in a single-player Creative-mode world, preferably Superflat for an unobstructed building area. Use an unmodified client without mods or resource packs. Keyboard and mouse instructions assume default controls.
preconditions: Launch the first version listed as affected, Minecraft 15w34c; do not use the fix version 23w35a.
Use a Creative-mode world so the required building materials can be obtained without crafting or exploration.
Prepare one Lever, one Redstone Dust, one Redstone Comparator, one Dragon Head, and at least four full solid support blocks such as Stone.
The comparator must begin in its default comparison mode and must not be right-clicked to toggle its mode after it has been powered.
The circuit must be initially unpowered before the trigger action: the lever is off, the redstone dust is dark, and the comparator is not outputting a signal.

Minecraft 15w34c predates the piglin head, so this primary reproduction tests the dragon-head case. The piglin-head case requires repeating the same comparator-output arrangement in an affected version that contains piglin heads, such as 22w46a.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for the exact Java Edition snapshot listed as “Minecraft 15w34c,” then launch that installation. Do not select 23w35a or a newer fixed version.
steps.exact_input: Minecraft 15w34c
steps.success_cue: The game reaches the title screen and the displayed version is 15w34c.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, and set the game mode to Creative. For a simple unobstructed build area, open More World Options and select the Superflat world type, then create the world.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; World Type: Superflat
steps.success_cue: The player spawns in a Creative-mode world with a clear area available for building.

steps.action: Wait before building until nearby terrain has rendered and normal movement and camera input respond without world-loading pauses.
steps.success_cue: The nearby ground is rendered, the player can move normally, and no terrain-loading screen is present.

steps.action: Press the inventory action key, which is E by default, to open the Creative inventory.
steps.exact_input: E
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open and includes item-category or item-search controls.

steps.action: Use the Creative inventory search field to locate the required items. Search for “lever” and place a Lever in the hotbar; search for “redstone” and place Redstone Dust in the hotbar; search for “comparator” and place a Redstone Comparator in the hotbar; search for “dragon” and place the Dragon Head in the hotbar; then obtain at least four Stone blocks or another full solid block. To move an item, left-click its Creative-inventory entry and then left-click an empty hotbar slot. When searching “redstone,” select the dust item rather than a torch or redstone block.
steps.exact_input: lever; redstone; comparator; dragon; stone
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains a Lever, Redstone Dust, a Redstone Comparator, a Dragon Head, and at least four full solid blocks.

steps.action: Press E or Esc to close the inventory and return control to the player.
steps.exact_input: E or Esc
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed and the crosshair is visible in the world.

steps.action: Select the solid blocks in the hotbar. On the open ground, place four support blocks in one straight horizontal row, with all four top surfaces at the same height. Treat the blocks in order as A, B, C, and D, where power will travel from A toward D.
steps.exact_input: right-click four times while targeting consecutive placement positions
steps.success_cue: Four solid blocks form a gapless straight row labeled conceptually A-B-C-D, with no height changes between them.

steps.action: Select the Lever and right-click the top surface of support block A to place it. Do not activate it after placement; if it was accidentally switched on, right-click it once to return it to the off position before continuing.
steps.exact_input: right-click the top of block A
steps.success_cue: A lever is attached to the top of block A and is in its off position.

steps.action: Select Redstone Dust and right-click the top surface of support block B, directly adjacent to the lever, to place one piece of dust.
steps.exact_input: right-click the top of block B
steps.success_cue: One unpowered, dark piece of redstone dust is present on block B between the lever position and the future comparator position.

steps.action: Select the Redstone Comparator. Stand on the A/B input side of the row, face along the row toward blocks C and D, and right-click the top surface of block C. The comparator must carry power from B toward D: its rear/input end is beside the redstone dust on B, and its front/output end points toward D. The side with the comparator’s single front torch should be closest to D. A powered comparator facing a mechanism component is the relevant direct-output arrangement. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AQuasi-connectivity?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: right-click the top of block C while facing from B toward D
steps.success_cue: The comparator sits on block C with its rear beside the redstone dust and its front/output end aimed directly at block D.

steps.action: Do not right-click the comparator after placing it. Confirm it remains in its default comparison mode; the mode-indicator/front torch should not be raised and continuously glowing as it would be in subtraction mode. If its mode was accidentally changed, break and replace the comparator in the same orientation while the lever remains off.
steps.success_cue: The comparator is correctly oriented, remains in default comparison mode, and is unpowered.

steps.action: Select the Dragon Head and right-click the top surface of support block D to place it immediately in front of the comparator. There must be no empty block between the comparator and the head.
steps.exact_input: right-click the top of block D
steps.success_cue: A floor-mounted Dragon Head is directly adjacent to the comparator’s front/output end.

steps.action: Check the complete circuit before triggering it. From input to output, it must be Lever on A, Redstone Dust on B, Redstone Comparator on C, and Dragon Head on D. Confirm the lever is off and the dust and comparator are unpowered. Do not test the circuit yet and do not toggle the comparator’s mode.
steps.success_cue: The four-part circuit is complete, correctly ordered, and still entirely unpowered.

steps.action: Move to the side of the circuit and aim the camera so the Dragon Head is clearly visible while the lever remains within right-click reach. Do not block the comparator-to-head connection and do not interact with the comparator.
steps.exact_input: W/A/S/D and mouse movement as needed
steps.success_cue: The player can clearly see the Dragon Head and can activate the lever without changing the comparator mode.

steps.action: Right-click the lever exactly once to switch it on. Do not right-click the comparator afterward. Immediately hand control to the observation subsystem while keeping the Dragon Head in view.
steps.exact_input: right-click the lever once
steps.success_cue: The lever is in its on position, the redstone dust is brightly powered, and the comparator is receiving and outputting power toward the adjacent Dragon Head.

stor.handoff_condition: The lever has just been switched on once, and the powered comparator is directly outputting into the adjacent Dragon Head while the comparator remains in its original comparison mode. The Dragon Head is visible on screen; begin observing its activation animation without further player interaction.
uncertainties: The report’s setup is supplied only through an attachment that was not available in the provided report text. The minimal straight-line circuit was reconstructed from the stated requirement that a lever activate a head through a comparator.

The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, coordinates, support-block material, or world type. Creative mode, Superflat terrain, and Stone supports are practical choices that do not replace the stated comparator-to-head condition.

The recommended first affected version, Minecraft 15w34c, contains the Dragon Head but predates the piglin head. Therefore the primary execution plan covers the dragon-head reproduction. To test the piglin-head addition separately, repeat steps 1-15 in 22w46a or another listed affected version containing Piglin Heads, substituting a Piglin Head for the Dragon Head.

The attachment may contain a different physical layout, but the reconstructed setup retains the essential reported signal path: an off-to-on lever transition powers redstone dust, the dust supplies the comparator’s rear input, and the comparator’s front output directly faces the head.
Do not use the report’s workaround of toggling the comparator mode while powered, because that is not part of the primary trigger and changes the state being tested.
